authors: Sarkar SN, Huang RQ, Logan SM, Yi KD, Dillon GH, Simpkins JW
title: Estrogens directly potentiate neuronal L-type Ca2+ channels
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
system: Embryonic rat hippocampal neurons, slices, and channel-transfected HEK293 cells; acute 17β-estradiol, including 10–1000 pM; nifedipine, estrogen-receptor antagonist and channel-mutant comparisons.
finding: Estradiol directly potentiated neuronal L-type calcium currents; pharmacology and a dihydropyridine-insensitive channel mutant localised the response to the channel.
scope: No RF exposure, contraceptive formulation or clinical fertility endpoint. Estradiol is not interchangeable with ethinylestradiol; increased physiological calcium signalling is not itself injury.

authors: Sun J, Chu Z, Moenter SM
title: Diurnal in vivo and rapid in vitro effects of estradiol on voltage-gated calcium channels in gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons
system: Adult ovariectomised female GnRH-GFP mice, with/without 0.625 µg estradiol implant; recordings 2–5 days later, morning versus afternoon. Acute bath estradiol 100 pM–100 nM.
finding: Prior estradiol lowered high-voltage-activated calcium currents in the morning and increased them in the afternoon; acute estradiol rapidly and reversibly potentiated currents through ERβ/L-type and GPR30/R-type contributions.
scope: A hormone-state and timing intervention, not an EMF×COC experiment. Rapid and prior in-vivo effects must be distinguished; no universal suppressive sign follows.
